name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with operable foot pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 motors engage only while the rider pedals and cut out at 20 and 28 mph; a Class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone, cutting out at 20 mph or when the brakes are applied (Connecticut General Statutes §14-1)

Not an electric bicycle if it has a throttle that can propel it past 20 mph in any mode, or is built or modified, by a switch, software or an app, to fall outside the definition; dirt bikes and ATVs are excluded too (Connecticut General Statutes §§14-1(31), 14-289n)

Carries a conspicuous label, in at least 9-point type, stating its class, top speed and motor wattage, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289l, as amended by Public Act 25-159)

Anyone who modifies its speed or motor engagement must replace the label to match, or remove it if the bike no longer qualifies as an e-bike (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289l, as amended by Public Act 25-159)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289l)
Every rider and passenger, of any age and on any class, must wear a bicycle helmet meeting ANSI, CPSC, ASTM or Snell standards (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289k)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289k)
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, unless a local ordinance bans it (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289k)

Class 1 may ride bicycle and multi-use trails and paths unless a local ordinance bans it; Class 2 is kept off natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized unless an ordinance allows it (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289k, as amended by Public Act 25-159)
Class 3 may not ride any bicycle or multi-use trail or path (Connecticut General Statutes §14-289k)
On a sidewalk or crosswalk it yields to pedestrians and sounds a warning before passing, and a town may ban riding there
Towns may regulate e-bike use by ordinance, including requiring annual licensing and registering sales
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle, motor-driven cycle or motorcycle, so needs no state registration or driver's license (Connecticut General Statutes §§14-1, 14-289k)

An electric bike that doesn't qualify, with a seat at least 26 inches high and a motor of up to 3,700 watts, is a motor-driven cycle, which needs a driver's license and, under 21, a motorcycle helmet; with a bigger motor it is generally a motorcycle
